newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks seen firm on foreign-led buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks seen firm on foreign-led buying.

text.p: Jakarta stocks are seen remaining firm on foreign-led buying particularly in selected blue-chips, brokers said.

"Foreigners are likely to continue driving the market today as Indonesia is considered to be much more attractive than other countries in the region including Thailand, Malaysia and the Phillipines," one broker said.
Foreign-led buying pushed the Jakarta composite index up 6.67 points, or 0.95 percent, to 705.29 points on Monday.
Brokers said the market focus was likely to remain on selected blue-chips including Bank Internasional Indonesia, Astra and Gudang Garam.
The foreign-led buying was partly due to recent announcements of upward revisions in 1997 net profit forecasts, brokers said.
Other small-capitalised stocks that made modest gains included property firm Duta Pertiwi, kitchenware manufacturer Kedaung Indah and property firm Summarecon.
Brokers said the market was likely to stay firm the rest of the day, but it was unlikely to book strong gains as it did on Monday due to generally soft regional markets.
